questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “View Encapsulation”?
options: View Encapsulation helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
View Encapsulation means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
View Encapsulation removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
View Encapsulation should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
questions.answer_key: View Encapsulation helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: View Encapsulation is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Emulated encapsulation” in this lesson?
options: Treat “Emulated encapsulation” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Emulated encapsulation” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Emulated encapsulation” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Emulated encapsulation” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Emulated encapsulation” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Emulated encapsulation” under View Encapsulation. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “View Encapsulation”?
options: Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
